Fetizanan SP Secretary Dear Gentlemen/Mesdames: DILG Legal Opinion No. 42 S. 2015 NOV 2015 This refers to the Honorable Sanggunian's 08 April 2015 letter through its Secretary, Ms. Diwata H. Fetizanan, requesting this level's opinion concerning the release and utilization of the unexpended balances of the 5% Local Disaster Risk Reduction & Management Fund (LDRRMF) under a special trust account pursuant to Items 6.41 and 6.52 of the NDRRMC- DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-1, dated 25 March 2013, specifically on the following: "l. What is being requited to be revised, the AIP of the current year or the corresponding AIP of fiscal years 2011 up to 2014? 2. Whether or not the enactment and approval Of an appropriation ordinance authorizing the utilization of the unexpended balances Of 5% PDRRM Fund is still necessary prior to its actual utilization/disbursement? 3. Whether the Provincial Governor will submit a supplemental budget to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan relative to the utilization of accumulated unexpended balances of 70% DRRMFfrom 2011-2014? The unexpended LDRRMF shall accrue to a special trust fund solely for the purpose of supgx)rting disaster risk reduction and management activities Of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC) within the next five (5) years. The unexpended balances of the LDRRMF may be released and utilized for new expenditure items upon submission of a revised z 6.5 AIP as approved by the local sanggunian and Local Chief Executive (LCE) upon recommendation of the LDRRMC in accordance with the approved LD RRMP.

Allegedly, the Provincial Government of Oriental Mindoro has accumulated unexpended balances of its Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund (PDRRMF) from 2011-2014 under special trust account. One of the requirements for the release and utilization of the unexpended balances of the LDRRMF pursuant to Paragraph 6.5 of NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-1, dated 25 March 2013, is the submission of a revised AIP as approved by the local sanggunian. The approved Annual Investment Program (AIP) is operationalized through the enactment of an appropriation ordinance authorizing the budget for the effective implementation of PPAs under said investment program. Thus, the General Fund Annual Budget of each LGU is supported with approved Investment Program embodying the PPAs for DRRM. The provincial government now intends to utilize the accumulated unexpended balances of its PDRRMF. Hence, this request. The following are the discussions relative to your queries: The Unex nded Balan e of th LDRRMF Pursuant to the 3rd paragraph of Section 21 of Republic Act No. 10121, the unexpended LDRRMF shall accrue to a special trust fund solely for the purpose of supporting disaster risk reduction and management activities of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Councils (LDRRMCs) within the next five (5) years. The LDRRMCs shall decide on the use of the unexpended balances of the LDRRMF which shall be incorporated in the Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP)3. The annually prepared LDRRMFIP or LDRRM Plan for the DRRM program shall present the following: the 30% allocation for Quick Response Fund (QRF) in lump-sum; the allocation for disaster mitigation, prevention and preparedness with details as to projects and activities to be funded; and under a separate caption, the list of projects and activities charged to the unexpended LDRRMF of previous years4. Paragraph 4.4, COA Circular NO. 2012-002, dated 12 September 2012. Citing paragraph 5.1.2, COA Circular NO. 2012-002. Page 2 of 4 DILG Opinion

The release and use of the LDRRMF shall be supported by the following documents5: 1) ForQRF 2) For projects and activities listed in the : approved plan as incorporated in the a) Local Sanggunian Resolution; and b) Declaration of State of Calamity. a) LDRRMFIP/LDRRMP local development plan and annual work and financial plan The LDRRMFIP[LDRRMP shall be reviewed and updated annually to include the activities to be funded from the unexpended QRF and DRRMF-MOOE of the previous years which were transferred to the Special Trust Fund6. The LDRRMFIP/LDRRMP is incorporated in the AIP, which refers to the annual slice of the Local Development Investment Program (LDIP)7 that constitutes the total resource requirements for all programs, projects and activities (PPAs) consisting of the annual capital expenditure and regular operating requirements of the LGU8. The ual Inv The AIP, is prepared and approved during the fiscal year before budget preparation as mandated under Article 41() of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of R.A. No. 7160. The AIP, therefore, is the yearly program of expenditures both for capital and current operating requirements of the LGU that will serve as basis for the preparation of Annual and Supplemental Budgets.9 s Citing Paragraph 5.13, id. s paragraph 5.1.15, id. 'The LDIP is as basic document linking the local plan to the budget. It contains a prioritized list of PPAs which are derived from the Comprehensive Development Plan (COP) in the case Of cities and municipalities, and the Provincial Development and physical Framework Plan (PDPFP) in the case Of provinces, matched with financing resources, and to be implemented annually within a three to six-year period. The first three (3) years Of the I-DIP shall be firmed up along with the priorities Of the incumbent LCEs. (DBM.NEDA-DILG-DOF JMC NO. 1, s. 2007. DILG-NEDA-DBM-DOF IMC No. 1, s. 2007; DEM. Budget Operations Manual far Local Government units (2008 Edition). p. 21. DBM. Budget Operations Manual for Local Government Units Edition). p. 21. Page 3 of 4 DILG Opinion

Utili o LD e Un Pursuant to NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC 2013-1, the unexpended balances of the LDRRMF may be released and utilized for authorized new expenditure items upon submission of the revised AIP of the current year considering that the basis for the preparation of the LGU's annual and supplemental budget is the current year's AIP. Precedure (ot Release and (Irilization of the Unexpended Balances of the LDRRMF The LDRRMFIP/LDRRMP is prepared and submitted by the Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Office (LDRRMO) to the LDRRMC for approval, which is in turn submitted by the latter to the Local Development Council (LDC) for deliberation and inclusion in the AIP, subject to LCE and local sanggunian approval. The approved AIP is operationalized in the LGU's annual budget or supplemental budget that is submitted by the LCE for approval of the sanggunian through an ordinance. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A.
